comparator.name: Academic Programme in Teaching Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: 2026–2027 OER Appendix 5 establishes the Radboud BSc within ALPO:120 EC of university courses over four years (34+31+25+30), plus 60 EC exemption grounded in the parallel HAN Pabo curriculum. This is not the combined 240 EC workload or the separate 240 EC Pabo diploma. Onderwijs selects Kwaliteit van onderwijs and Vormgeven van onderwijs (4 EC each), followed by Beroepsvaardigheden 3 onderwijs en pedagogiek (8 EC). There is no free elective space (Art 9.5). Appendix 5 visibly repeats PWB 3370 Samenwerken met professionals twice; it is one identical 4 EC code, counted once, consistent with the stated 30 EC fourth-year total and current official year 4 list. Art 8.2 requires academic-skills 1 before 2, professional-skillsALPO before 3 and academic-skills 2 before the thesis; pre-enrolment also applies to thesis and professional-skills 3. Complete earlier-year requirements in this ordinary pathway. Appendix 6 requires 24 of 34 RU EC in year 1 for a positive RU BSA; HAN currently describes its own advice as nonbinding PSA, so no second binding threshold is asserted. RADAr academic Dutch is a 0 EC year 1 obligation on the current year page and is recorded separately rather than added to the 180 EC.

core: Child development across motor, cognitive, language, social, emotional and moral domains
Pedagogy, upbringing, learning and primary education
Educational and developmental research, analysis and academic skills
Developmental and learning problems, orthopedagogy, assessment and treatment
Educational quality, curriculum design and professional teaching practice
adjacent: Psychology and neuroscience of cognition, behaviour, language and emotion
Child wellbeing, mental health and developmental disorders
Social, ethical and professional contexts of upbringing and education
questions: How do children develop and learn from birth to adulthood?
How can research improve education and evidence-based professional decisions?
How can developmental and learning difficulties be identified and supported?

trace: Direct foundations: nature–nurture, mental processes, brain function and psychological/neuroscientific methods ground study of typical and atypical development.

Complementary method: data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and an independent data-analysis project supply concrete skills for empirical developmental and educational questions; the datasets are not necessarily educational.
Complementary academic skill: argument structure, academic essays and oral presentation support research communication and provide preparation for designing primary-school speaking activities.
Direct psychological foundations: theories of social influence on thoughts, feelings and behaviour support analysis of relationships and social development; the course is not child-specific.

Direct method: research design, sampling, experimental/survey techniques and descriptive/inferential statistics support developmental and educational inquiry; a general group project is not a teaching placement.

Complementary neuroscience: comparative anatomy, biorhythms, animal models, research ethics and experimental laboratory techniques help interpret biological evidence about behaviour; it is not a human child-development course.

Complementary normative study: moral theories, responsibility and equality support critical decisions involving children and educational practice; no dedicated Dutch child/education-law syllabus is claimed.

Direct quantitative method: regression, factor analysis, covariance models and logistic/nonparametric analyses support behavioural evidence and measurement questions; not a complete psychometrics and decision-science course.

Complementary biological foundation: cells, inheritance, physiology and cellular communication ground the programme’s study of biological influences on development and prepare for adult physiology; this is not child pedagogy.

Direct cognition: memory, emotion, attention, social cognition and experimental reasoning address mechanisms underlying learning and development; the syllabus is not specifically developmental neuropsychology.

Complementary health psychology: biopsychosocial explanations of stress, health behaviour and chronic illness support analysis of wellbeing and vulnerability across the lifespan, including their consequences for development.
Direct cognitive mechanisms: sensory processing and goal-directed action inform understanding of perceptual/motor functioning; not the comparator’s dedicated child motor-development course.

Direct psychopathology: lifespan disorders, developmental pathways, culture, assessment and treatment perspectives include infants, children and adolescents; not specialised orthopedagogical practice.

Direct developmental core: physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from prenatal life through adulthood, including childhood and adolescence, substantially responds to the target’s defining developmental questions.

Direct, bounded educational application: students design and teach speaking/debating exercises to primary pupils aged 9–12 in a community-engaged course; it is not a full Pabo placement or general didactics sequence.

Direct, bounded educational application: research and evidence-based materials for youth leaders and educators address democratic school culture, supportive learning environments, empathy and mental wellbeing; not a general special-needs curriculum.

Complementary social analysis: institutions, social interaction, inequality, race, gender and class support interpretation of the social environments in which upbringing and learning occur; not sociology of education as a dedicated syllabus.

Complementary communication: framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and persuasion ethics support critical interpretation of influence and responsible public communication about development and learning; the institutional project need not concern schools.

Complementary physiological foundation: adult organ systems, homeostasis, integration, metabolism, growth and ageing support understanding of biological functioning and bodily influences on development; not a paediatric or child motor-development course.

Direct research method: systematic reviews, meta-analysis, effect sizes and R support evidence-based developmental/educational judgments; it synthesises existing studies and does not supply the comparator’s separate primary-research thesis.

Direct cognition/language: acquisition, reading/dyslexia, bilingualism, comprehension and language impairments respond to the target’s cognitive/language and learning questions; not language-teaching didactics.

Direct clinical perspective: psychological assessment and psychotherapies across age groups, including children, provide evidence and ethical frameworks for developmental-support questions; no practitioner competence or orthopedagogy qualification is implied.

Direct research method: qualitative design, collection, interpretation, reflexivity and group inquiry support the study of educational relationships and practice; topics are not guaranteed to be educational.

routeSelection.basis: The generic ALPO bachelor combines pedagogical science with primary teaching. Onderwijs most directly represents this defining identity through educational quality and curriculum design. It is selected independently of UCR fit; the formal source confirms all four specialisations and the corresponding professional-skills choices.

selection.assessment: Stop at one. The strongest developmental-support content is now included in the closest programme: lifespan and abnormal psychology, clinical assessment and therapy perspectives, language, youth resilience and empirical methods. The old second programme achieved difference mainly through evolution, cellular biology, molecular pathology, laboratory work, infection, immunity and organ disease. Those subjects do not implement a distinct orthopedagogical or learning-support curriculum. No credible separate 24-course developmental-support programme can be formed by padding this limited content; simple removal or reshuffling would not establish qualitative distinctness. Educational quality and curriculum design remains a genuine but infeasible further direction because dedicated educational evaluation, curriculum and didactics courses are absent.

alternatives.label: Developmental psychology, cognition & learning
alternatives.labelReason: Psychology, cognition, language and methods dominate the completed programme. School engagement is specific to applied rhetoric and youth resilience; this label does not imply a dedicated education-science or teacher-training degree.
alternatives.concept: A programme studying typical and atypical human development through developmental, social and clinical psychology, cognition and language, supported by biological foundations, ethical reasoning and empirical research. Applied rhetoric with primary-school pupils and youth-focused educational research connect part of this study to learning environments.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour and data foundations precede advanced psychology, cognition, quantitative analysis and evidence synthesis. Rhetoric precedes the primary-school practice course and persuasive communication; the life-science gateway precedes physiology. Introductory sociology precedes qualitative inquiry. Psycholinguistics is assigned to 2029h 1, its available late-cycle term. Every formal prerequisite and assigned offering is checked directly from the workbook.

blocks: Partial correspondence in higher cognition and brain–behaviour research; UCR does not reproduce a dedicated clinical/developmental neuropsychology syllabus.
Both address perception and action or motor functioning; UCR approaches these processes through cognitive neuroscience rather than a child-development sequence.
Partial developmental correspondence: childhood and adolescent social/emotional development within a lifespan course; not a dedicated moral-development course.
Both examine links between cognition and language; UCR provides an advanced psycholinguistic treatment rather than the comparator's developmental course.

UCR has no single scheduled course that directly reproduces Leerproblemen.

UCR has no single scheduled course that directly reproduces Ontwikkelingsproblemen.

UCR includes general and psychological statistics, but no separate four-course Analyse sequence corresponding component by component.
UCR's quantitative methods are represented by Research Methods & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods; there is no second directly equivalent component.
UCR does not reproduce the comparator's third sequenced analysis course as a separate required component.
UCR does not reproduce the comparator's fourth sequenced analysis course as a separate required component.
Required 10 EC ALPO bachelor thesis. The scheduled UCR seminar teaches evidence synthesis; optional independent research is separate from the 24-course programme.
Both develop academic argument, writing and oral presentation, while UCR uses rhetoric as its organising framework.
Both develop structured ethical reasoning for difficult professional decisions, though UCR is not specific to Dutch child and education law.

One 7.5 EC course involves teaching speaking and debating to primary-school pupils. It corresponds only to a small part of the school-practice context underlying the 60 EC exemption; it does not replace the Pabo curriculum.
UCR has no single scheduled course that directly reproduces Wetenschapsfilosofie.
UCR has communication and professional-development courses but no ALPO professional-practice sequence combining pedagogical science and teacher education.
UCR has no single scheduled course that directly reproduces Academische vaardigheden 2 ALPO.
UCR offers social-science analysis of institutions but no dedicated course in evaluating educational quality.
UCR's applied primary-school rhetoric course includes activity design, but it does not reproduce a general curriculum-design course and is aligned to the broader Pabo exemption.
UCR has no single scheduled course that directly reproduces Samenwerken met professionals.
UCR has no advanced professional-practice component equivalent to the ALPO education-and-pedagogy route.

notes.text: This UCR programme offers substantial developmental psychology, cognition, language and research, with specific work involving primary pupils and youth learning environments. ALPO also provides dedicated pedagogy, education science, curriculum design, sustained professional practice and subject didactics through the linked Pabo. UCR does not reproduce that teaching curriculum or award its professional qualification. Its evidence-synthesis seminar is not the required ALPO bachelor thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: ALPO combines Radboud’s Pedagogical Sciences degree with primary-teacher education at HAN over four years. Students study typical and atypical child development, upbringing, learning and research, alongside subject didactics and school practice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR programme offers a related academic route through developmental psychology, cognition, language and research, with limited direct school engagement. It provides less dedicated pedagogy, education science and professional practice than ALPO, and does not qualify students as primary-school teachers.

curriculum.limitation: The Radboud degree comprises 120 EC of university courses plus 60 EC of exemption based on the parallel HAN Pabo curriculum. This table represents the 180 EC Radboud degree, rather than the combined workload of both qualifications.
